Sam Altman runs OpenAI, the company that put ChatGPT into the world's hands. He sits with Tucker Carlson for a conversation that moves between God and Elon Musk. It also touches the mysterious death of a former employee of his company. The range is unusual even for Carlson's show.

Altman's public manner is careful, which makes his turns here, on faith and on questions around the employee's death, the more notable. Carlson presses on the power Altman holds and the beliefs that guide it. The episode preserves a rare long-form hearing with the man steering the most consequential technology of the decade, talking about subjects his press appearances usually avoid. Listeners can judge his answers, and his evasions, for themselves.

Vivek Ramaswamy tells Tucker Carlson that Americans can handle the truth about September 11 in this episode. Ramaswamy, an entrepreneur who ran for president, built his campaign on blunt claims about hidden government stories. Here he presses for full honesty about the attacks and what led to them.

The two discuss unanswered questions about foreign links, intelligence failures, and sealed records. Ramaswamy argues that public trust dies when officials hide hard facts. Carlson asks what a full release of records would change. The episode is a call for disclosure on the darkest day in modern American life.
